evidence.description: The authentication handler registers a visit or resets seeds without updating the published authentication and profile properties.
Subsequent authentication and profile synchronization occurs in the separate profile-update handler, with isLoggedIn further deferred into a task.
The refresh path depends on the potentially stale isLoggedIn property.

candidates.explanation: Authentication-change notifications do not synchronize isLoggedIn, userProfile, username, or avatarURL. These values are initialized once and subsequently updated only by the separate profile-update handler. Consequently, a login or logout notification alone leaves the published authentication state stale, and refreshSeedState can choose the wrong collection path. The authStateLoaded action also performs no synchronization despite its comment.
candidates.title: Authentication events leave published authentication state stale

evidence.description: The request captures an access token, awaits the backend, and unconditionally applies the response or error without cancellation or session validation.
Applying a response mutates the displayed level, progress, and seed balance.
Logout resets local state but does not invalidate pending visit requests.

candidates.explanation: Each visit registration launches an independent task and applies its result after suspension without checking whether the authentication session changed or a newer request completed. A response arriving after logout can overwrite the reset guest balance and level with authenticated account data. Concurrent refreshes can also apply responses out of order, and failures can set the error flag for a session that is no longer active.
candidates.title: Pending visit requests can overwrite newer session state

evidence.description: Each animation schedules an unconditional delayed seed assignment and a separate delayed clearing of the shared increment property.
Logout assigns a new local seed count without cancelling previously scheduled animation closures.

candidates.explanation: Balance updates are deferred using uncancelled closures that retain their target values. A newer update or logout reset can occur before a queued closure runs, after which the older closure overwrites the current seed count. Overlapping animations also schedule independent clearing callbacks, allowing an earlier animation to clear a later animation's balanceIncrement prematurely.
candidates.title: Uncoordinated animation callbacks overwrite newer balance state

evidence.description: The nonisolated shared property initializes the main-actor-isolated provider inside assumeIsolated without an actor hop.

candidates.explanation: The shared instance is explicitly accessible without main-actor isolation, but its lazy initializer uses MainActor.assumeIsolated. That operation checks isolation rather than moving execution to the main actor. First access from outside the main actor can therefore fail the isolation check instead of safely initializing the singleton.
candidates.title: Nonisolated singleton access relies on main-actor execution
